A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GuidedSceneGen. Their text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original panorama-generation and 3D-reconstruction evaluations, ablations, alignment measurements and a 31-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a trajectory-planning comparison in Appendix F and Table 5.

M1.justification: The proxy-generation, guided panorama, trajectory-alignment and 3DGS procedures remain unchanged, including their losses and camera-scale search. Appendix F introduces comparison planners without replacing the proposed heuristic.

E1.justification: The training datasets, Structured3D evaluation and indoor generation tasks remain unchanged. The planning comparison uses the existing indoor-layout setting, and multi-room expansion was already demonstrated in v1.

E2.justification: New Table 5 evaluates standard mesh-based view planning and its depth-filtered variant against the proposed trajectory heuristic. The panorama and full-scene comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds a planner-comparison protocol using four 42-frame quadrant trajectories and reporting scene coverage alongside MEt3R. This extends evaluation without revising the existing training or benchmark settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused trajectory-planning ablation examining coverage versus reconstruction consistency, including the effect of depth filtering. Existing guidance, loss and camera-scale analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The user study retains 31 participants, 2945 data points, ANOVA F=113 with p<0.05, and pairwise significance at p<0.00833. No new repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports MEt3R/coverage of 0.029/74.29% for standard planning, 0.027/60.01% with depth filtering, and 0.024/62.39% for the proposed method. Tables 1–4 retain their values. Figure 12 adds qualitative walkthrough frames.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, the loss definitions and Algorithm 1 retain their mathematical content. The new planning comparison supplies procedural descriptions and empirical evidence without adding formal assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about absolute scale, semantic interpretability, trajectory efficiency and seamless expansion. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly argues that maximizing coverage can reduce the overlap needed for reconstruction, explaining the consistency–coverage tradeoff. Its statement that the proposed method achieves the 'highest MEt3R' conflicts with Table 5, where lower is better and its score is lowest.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and implementation descriptions for the new planners, including occupancy grids, visibility tests, greedy selection, A* traversal and frame resampling. Existing model and training details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds WorldPrompter and SpatialGen, expands discussion of the already-cited Voyager, and sharpens distinctions concerning conditioning and proxy geometry. Numerous bibliography updates concern the same works, including consolidation of the duplicate ControlRoom3D reference.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, shortens some headings, standardizes bibliography entries and inserts the trajectory-ablation appendix. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and the walkthrough montage in Figure 12. The existing scene-expansion diagram moves from v1 Figure 11 in the appendix to v2 Figure 7 in the main text; retained figures and tables also receive size and placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: Appendix F provides useful empirical support for the trajectory-design choice, while expanded related work and walkthrough frames improve context and visible evidence. These are limited gains with the method and principal results unchanged. The new 'highest MEt3R' wording introduces a small clarity defect, but does not outweigh the added evidence.
